data.name: Kinna
data.gender_notes: Kinna is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew word כנה (kinnah), meaning 'grace, beauty'. In the Bible, the name Kinna appears in the book of 1 Samuel, where it is given to the concubine of King Jephthah. After Jephthah vowed to offer a burnt offering to the Lord if he was granted victory, he returned home to find his daughter in the house. In an attempt to keep his vow, he offered her to his friends instead. They took her, raped her, and killed her. Upon hearing the news, Jephthah was filled with sorrow and mourned his daughter for 2 months. The name Kinna is a reminder of the grace and beauty that can be found in even the most tragic of circumstances.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of grace and beauty in the face of adversity
data.etymology: Kinna belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Grace, beauty.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kinna total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

This name's presence in Scripture contributes to its significance in religious and secular contexts, imparting a tangible connection to a time when the ancient Israelites navigated their lives in a culture influenced by the stories, laws, and values of the Hebrew Bible.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Kinna lies in its capacity to evoke emotions and thoughts that can inspire hope and resilience. The Hebrew word כנה (kinnah) not only indicates grace and beauty but also underscores the depth of human suffering and loss. This spiritual meaning captured most poignantly in the story of Jephthah's concubine, Kinna, whose tragic end has left a profound impact on many readers throughout history. As a reminder of the divine grace that shines through adversity and the enduring inner beauty of the human spirit, the name Kinna is an eloquent expression of our capacity to find redemption and hope even amid the darkest moments of our lives.
